# Native Shell (NSH)

**Build once, native everywhere.** Native Shell is a native UI framework for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows,
Linux and the web, built in Rust. It unifies components, state, logic and API, with app-owned visual design and
platform rendering: native views on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux, HTML on the web, GPUI in GPUI apps,
character Cells in a terminal, with the platform's own text, input and interaction (a menu is a popup on the desktop
and a sheet on a phone). Write the app in TSX and extend it with Rust components, modules and classes through nshm
crates, or write the whole app in Rust.

<img width="1200" alt="image" src="https://nsh.dev/versions/main/brand/nsh-banner-dark.png" />

Package it as a standalone app on every platform, or embed it in an existing one. On the same engine, apps load TSX
modules at run time — plugins, features, UI generated by AI — delivered as signed packages and run in a sandbox the
host configures.

Documentation, guides and live demos: **[nsh.dev](https://nsh.dev)**.

## Goals

Native views and interaction, with an app-owned design: NSH shares components, state and APIs across platforms,
while the app controls colors, typography, spacing, shapes and motion. `nsh/base` provides the behavior and accessible
structure of common controls such as `Button`, `Checkbox` and `Switch`; apps and community libraries give them a look.
Platform modules expose capabilities specific to their platforms, such as the mobile system tab bar.

Read [Goals and design principles](https://nsh.dev/docs/goals) for the component boundaries and how these goals guide
Rust apps, TSX modules and AI-generated UI.

## Features

- Write apps in TSX, extend them with Rust through nshm crates (the app's own in `ext/`, or published ones), or write
  them entirely in Rust, and render with each platform's own UI, sharing the same reactive engine, flexbox and grid
  layout, system text, input and accessibility.
- Give your app its own look: NSH provides the primitives, Tailwind classes, a theme and an unstyled UI foundation
  (`nsh/base`: navigation, safe areas, dialogs, the keyboard, the status bar), and your app draws its components from
  them in TSX or Rust.
- Embed in existing native apps alongside components such as maps and web views, or package as standalone apps
  and static websites.
- Deliver TSX screens at run time with signed packages and host-controlled sandbox capabilities.
- Build AI-generated screens with TSX and Tailwind, generated TypeScript declarations and
  [model-readable documentation](https://nsh.dev/llms.txt).
- Iterate with TSX hot updates, headless tracing and a single Rust-built `nsh` CLI for building and packaging.

### Platforms

| Platform | Drawn with | Embed with | Requires |
|---|---|---|---|
| iOS | UIKit, CoreText | `NshAppView` (Swift, `NativeShell.xcframework`) | iOS 15+ |
| Android | Android views, `StaticLayout` | `NshView` (Java / Kotlin, `nsh.aar`) | Android 8 (API 26)+ |
| macOS | AppKit, Core Animation, CoreText | `AppView` (Rust, `nsh-platform-macos`) | macOS 14+ |
| Windows | Win32, Direct2D, DirectWrite | `AppView` (Rust, `nsh-platform-windows`) | Windows 10 1809+ |
| Linux | GTK 4, Pango | `AppView` (Rust, `nsh-platform-linux`) | GTK 4.14+ |
| GPUI (macOS, Windows, Linux) | GPUI (GPUI Fast) | `AppView` (Rust, a GPUI view, `nsh-platform-gpui`) | macOS, Windows; Linux with Vulkan |
| Terminal | ratatui, the terminal's Cell grid | `AppView` (Rust, an area of a ratatui frame, `nsh-platform-tui`) | Terminals on macOS, Windows, Linux |
| Web | HTML, CSS | `createPlayer` (JavaScript) or an iframe | Modern browsers |

Each desktop runs and packages apps with its own backend (AppKit, Win32, GTK 4). The GPUI backend draws with GPUI on
all three desktops and embeds NSH in GPUI and GPUI Kit apps; `nsh run --target gpui` shows an app as they do. The web
platform (`nsh run --target web`, `nsh package --target web`) publishes apps as static sites and runs the website's
live demos.
The terminal backend (`nsh run --target tui`) draws apps on a terminal's character grid in its own colors, with the
keyboard and the mouse.

## Quick start

Install the `nsh` command ([other ways](https://nsh.dev/docs/installation)):

<details open>
<summary>macOS / Linux</summary>

```sh
curl -fsSL https://nsh.dev/install.sh | sh
```

The nightly build of the latest `main`, rebuilt every night that it changes:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://nsh.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --nightly
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Homebrew</summary>

```sh
brew install longbridge/tap/nsh
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>MacPorts</summary>

```sh
sudo port install native-shell
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Windows (PowerShell)</summary>

```powershell
irm https://nsh.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

The nightly build:

```powershell
$env:NSH_VERSION = 'nightly'; irm https://nsh.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>From source (macOS / Linux)</summary>

Build and install the latest `main` from source (Git, Rust and the
[platform build dependencies](https://nsh.dev/docs/installation) required):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://nsh.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --source
```

Re-run to update. The checkout stays in `~/.nsh/source` for runtime builds.

</details>

Choose how to write your app:

| | TSX | TSX extended with Rust | Rust |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create | `nsh init my-app --template ts` | `nsh init my-app --template mixed` | `nsh init my-app --template rust` |
| Write | TSX components, Tailwind classes and signals | TSX screens, importing components, modules and classes from the app's nshm crate in `ext/` | Rust components, typed styles and signals |
| Iterate | Hot updates that preserve state | TSX hot; Rust changes restart | Rebuild and restart on Rust changes |
| Toolchain | `nsh` | `nsh` and [Rust](https://rustup.rs) | `nsh` and [Rust](https://rustup.rs) |

`nsh init` starts a TSX app by default. When the app needs Rust (a parser, a storage engine, a native view, heavy
computation), add an nshm crate in `ext/` or a published one, and TSX imports it with types generated from the Rust
signatures; see [nshm](https://nsh.dev/docs/nshm). A whole app in Rust ships with no JavaScript VM; see
[Building with Rust](https://nsh.dev/docs/rust). Rust builds work with the standard Cargo or
[huacnlee/cargo](https://github.com/huacnlee/cargo).

Run the app on your chosen platform:

<details>
<summary>iOS</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target ios        # iOS simulator; requires Xcode
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Android</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target android    # emulator or device; requires the Android SDK
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>macOS</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target macos      # AppKit window
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Windows</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target windows    # Win32 window
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Linux</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target linux      # GTK 4 window
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>GPUI (macOS, Windows, Linux)</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target gpui       # as GPUI apps that embed it show it
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Terminal</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target tui        # in the current terminal
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Web</summary>

```sh
nsh run my-app --target web        # open in the browser
```

</details>

The TSX template includes `App.tsx`, `nsh.json` and `tsconfig.json`, with generated TypeScript declarations in
`.nsh/types` for your editor. The mixed template adds an nshm crate in `ext/<name>-native`. The Rust template includes
a Cargo project with its root component in `src/lib.rs`.
Logs and errors show in the terminal. What each platform needs:
[Installation](https://nsh.dev/docs/installation#platform-tools).

## Examples

| Example | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [`examples/gallery`](examples/gallery) | A tour of what NSH supports: lists, navigation, forms, controls, gestures, animation, images, styles, text, web view and video, `fetch` |
| [`examples/counter`](examples/counter) | The smallest app |
| [`examples/tasks`](examples/tasks) | A small app with a store, pages, a list, a system alert and tests, laid out as the Coding Guides say |
| [`examples/rust-exports`](examples/rust-exports) | A TSX app using a component, a module and a class of its own Rust crate |
| [`examples/hopper`](examples/hopper) | A dark, tabbed dashboard built only from primitives: interactive canvas charts, sliders, menus, animation |
| [`examples/desktop`](examples/desktop) | A desktop app with a title bar and menus of its own (`nsh/desktop`) |
| [`examples/embed-ios`](examples/embed-ios), [`examples/embed-android`](examples/embed-android) | NSH inside existing native apps, with a native component the app registers |
| [`examples/tasks-rs`](examples/tasks-rs) | The same tasks app written only in Rust |
| [`examples/gallery-rs`](examples/gallery-rs) | The gallery written in Rust: an app with no TSX and no QuickJS |
| [`examples/bench`](examples/bench) | Rust components against the same components in TSX |

```sh
cargo run
```

## Skills for AI coding agents

Install the NSH skills for your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others), so it follows
NSH's model in TSX, TSX extended with Rust, or Rust:

```sh
npx skills add longbridge/nsh
```

| Skill | What it gives the agent |
|---|---|
| [`nsh`](skills/nsh/SKILL.md) | Building apps in TSX, TSX extended with Rust nshm crates, or Rust: the Coding Guides, a page per mode, tooling, and a tested app in TSX and in Rust |
| [`nsh-design-guides`](skills/nsh-design-guides/SKILL.md) | The Design Guides, for any screen, interaction or interface copy |

## Acknowledgements

NSH builds on the ideas of these projects:

- [GPUI](https://gpui.rs), Zed's UI framework: the typed units and geometry (`Points`, `Point`, `Size`,
  `Bounds`, `Edges`), `SharedString`, typed styles in Rust and much of the vocabulary of NSH's API.
- [GPUI Kit](https://gpui-kit.com): `gpui-base`'s unstyled base components, which `nsh-base`
  follows in names and scope, and the Coding and Design Guides.
- [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com): the design tokens of NSH's theme, its default theme (`neutral`) and the
  `cssVars` theme files apps write or export from shadcn's themes and tweakcn.
- [Solid](https://solidjs.com): the reactive graph, signals, memos, effects, owners and context, which both the
  Rust and the TSX side of NSH run on.
